Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Our third quarter showed both engines of this company at work: a data-center cooling franchise that keeps compounding, and a commercial business we are managing with speed and discipline.

At the same time, we moved fast on the two things that weighed on our commercial results. We initiated a voluntary recall of our GV-400 series combination gas valve under the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's Fast Track program - a proactive, customer-first decision we would make again. And we accelerated Project Keystone, our program to structurally lower our cost base, which is on track to deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, and adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, with adjusted EPS of $0.15. The commercial side of our business absorbed a difficult quarter; what we control - winning data-center programs, building backlog, and acting on cost - moved forward.

## Highlights
- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; data-center cooling backlog up 22.0% to a record $574.2 million.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed proactively with the CPSC under the Fast Track program; replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since late September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS exclude the GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs; GAAP results are presented in the KPI summary table accompanying this letter.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by hyperscale demand for our liquid-cooling portfolio. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, introduced last quarter with two hyperscale customers, ramped through Q3, and the two new hyperscale awards won this quarter extend our content with marquee customers - a validation of the CR-9 platform and of the engineering behind our liquid-cooling portfolio. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. These programs convert on multi-quarter build cycles, which supports revenue through late FY2026 and FY2027 and gives us visibility that few companies our size can match. Our capital spending remains oriented to the capacity and test infrastructure this backlog requires.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and the pause of GV-400 orders by several OEM customers pending the recall notice. On the recall itself: it was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program. In commercial HVAC, we are managing for cost, price and mix until volumes recover, and Keystone gives that business a structurally better cost base to grow from.

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66 to $1.70 billion, from $1.78 to $1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205 to $215 million, from $255 to $270 million. The update reflects the softer commercial environment and recall-related order timing in BCV, partly offset by the continued strength of our data-center business.

Entering FY2027, the year builds in two ways: data-center backlog converts into revenue, and Keystone savings reach full run-rate. A record backlog and a lower structural cost base together give us confidence in the earnings recovery ahead.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash on hand. Our priorities are unchanged: convert backlog, deliver Keystone, and strengthen the company through earnings growth.

We want to thank our 6,200 employees - particularly our quality, manufacturing and field teams, who have worked around the clock on the recall and on our customers' builds this quarter. To our customers: your trust is the foundation of this company, and we will keep earning it with safe, reliable products and responsive service. And to you, our shareholders: the demand for what we build - efficient, high-performance thermal systems for the world's most demanding environments - has never been stronger. We intend to meet it.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe

Mark Ostrander

We initiated a voluntary recall of our GV-400 series combination gas valve under the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's Fast Track program - a proactive, customer-first decision we would make again. And we accelerated Project Keystone, our program to structurally lower our cost base, which is on track to deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, and adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, with adjusted EPS of $0.15. The commercial side of our business absorbed a difficult quarter; what we control - winning data-center programs, building backlog, and acting on cost - moved forward.

## Highlights
- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; data-center cooling backlog up 22.0% to a record $574.2 million.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed proactively with the CPSC under the Fast Track program; replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since late September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS exclude the GV-400 recall charge and Project Keystone restructuring costs; GAAP results are presented in the KPI summary table accompanying this letter.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by hyperscale demand for our liquid-cooling portfolio. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, introduced last quarter with two hyperscale customers, ramped through Q3, and the two new hyperscale awards won this quarter extend our content with marquee customers - a validation of the CR-9 platform and of the engineering behind our liquid-cooling portfolio. TDC backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. These programs convert on multi-quarter build cycles, which supports revenue through late FY2026 and FY2027 and gives us visibility that few companies our size can match. Our capital spending remains oriented to the capacity and test infrastructure this backlog requires.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and the pause of GV-400 orders by several OEM customers pending the recall notice. On the recall itself: it was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program. Our teams identified the root cause, completed corrective action with the supplier, and have been shipping replacement valves since late September. In the third quarter we recorded a $21.6 million reserve covering field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. We expect paused orders to resume as remediation progresses. In commercial HVAC, we are managing for cost, price and mix until volumes recover, and Keystone gives that business a structurally better cost base to grow from.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66 to $1.70 billion, from $1.78 to $1.84 billion, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205 to $215 million, from $255 to $270 million. The update reflects the softer commercial environment and recall-related order timing in BCV, partly offset by the continued strength of our data-center business.

The heart of our margin recovery plan is Project Keystone: $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027 across our cost structure, with benefits building through FY2027. Combined with conversion of our record data-center backlog, we expect improving revenue and margin as FY2027 progresses, and we are managing free cash flow for improvement as recall spending rolls off and Keystone savings land. Entering FY2027, the year builds in two ways: data-center backlog converts into revenue, and Keystone savings reach full run-rate. A record backlog and a lower structural cost base together give us confidence in the earnings recovery ahead.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash on hand. Our priorities are unchanged: convert backlog, deliver Keystone, and strengthen the company through earnings growth.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees - particularly our quality, manufacturing and field teams, who have worked around the clock on the recall and on our customers' builds this quarter. To our customers: your trust is the foundation of this company, and we will keep earning it with safe, reliable products and responsive service. And to you, our shareholders: the demand for what we build - efficient, high-performance thermal systems for the world's most demanding environments - has never been stronger. We intend to meet it.

Sincerely,
